This state/province falls within the border-zone exception identified by a foreign home ministry's country-of-origin guidance (June 2025) and named in several foreign governments' travel advisories as a distinct zone for which travel is discouraged. One of those advisories specifically warns that visitors must obtain special permission from the interior authorities to enter certain areas. The director of an independent monitoring group for the zone states flatly that “there is no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people” there, and that even private existence can trigger violence, detention, or forced return to families, adding that “every year it gets worse.”

No separate written law specific to this state/province exists, and no purge on the scale of the zone's worst-hit neighbouring state/province has been documented here, but the same security-and-custom enforcement logic applies: the federal transition ban and propaganda statute operate in a context where local security structures and family-honour norms produce extrajudicial responses unmediated by legal process, and where special-access restrictions impede independent monitoring and foreign consular support. That places this state/province a large negative deviation below the country-wide average — well below the ordinary central states/provinces of the country (which sit at the country-wide average) because of the zone-exception designation, but above the one neighbouring state/province whose documented secret-prison and extrajudicial-killing infrastructure has no confirmed equivalent here.
